Export an obis_h3 store to hive-partitioned Parquet

Source: R/export.R
obis_h3_export_parquet.Rd

Writes the indicator layers of a store built by build_obis_h3_duckdb() to a directory of hive-partitioned Parquet files that a static web app can read directly with DuckDB-WASM (one small file per map layer and H3 resolution):

Usage

obis_h3_export_parquet(
  con,
  dir_out,
  release,
  res_decade = 1:5,
  res_year = 1:5,
  years = NULL,
  res_species = c(3L, 4L, 5L),
  species_decades = FALSE,
  heads = TRUE,
  res_heads = 1:7,
  parent_res = c(`6` = 2L, `7` = 3L),
  parent_res_taxon = c(`6` = 0L, `7` = 0L),
  parent_min_rows = 50000,
  max_open = EXPORT_MAX_OPEN,
  compression = "zstd",
  row_group_rows = 10000L,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  decades = seq(1960L, 2020L, by = 10L),
  esn = 50L,
  place_collections = NULL,
  place_exact = NULL,
  place_exact_occ = NULL,
  temp_dir = NULL,
  max_temp_dir_size = NULL,
  memory_limit = NULL,
  threads = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

con

connection from obis_store_connect() (read-only is fine).

dir_out

output directory; files go under dir_out/release/.

release

release tag, e.g. "v20260728" (the date of the OBIS sync the store was built from); recorded in release.json. Its obis_snapshot is the environment variable OBIS_DATA_DATE (the newest OBIS object's date, which refresh_obis_h3.sh passes) when that is a YYYY-MM-DD date, else the date in the tag.

res_decade

H3 resolutions for the decade layers (default 1-5).

res_year

H3 resolutions for the year layers (default 1-5); integer(0) skips them.

years

years to export in the year layers; default NULL, every year present.

res_species

H3 resolutions of the species table (default 3, 4, 5); integer(0) skips it.

species_decades

also write the per-decade species table species_decade/ (default FALSE).

heads

write the pre-aggregated heads as taxon layers (default TRUE; needs the species table and the store's taxon table).

res_heads

the resolutions of the heads (default 1-7; res 6 and 7 are split by parent_res_taxon like the rank layers).

parent_res

named integer vector, fine resolution -> parent resolution, for the all and eov layers: those resolutions are written one file per parent cell (res=<r>/p=<parent>/). Default c("6" = 2L, "7" = 3L); NULL writes every resolution whole.

parent_res_taxon

the same for the taxon layer (default c("6" = 0L, "7" = 0L), the base cell).

parent_min_rows

a (layer key, res) with at most this many rows is written whole even when its res is in parent_res (default 50000).

max_open

no longer used (0.11.0): every file is written by its own COPY, so no more than one is open at a time. Kept so old calls still run.

compression

Parquet compression codec (default "zstd").

row_group_rows

rows per Parquet row group of the indicator layer files (default 10000; DuckDB rounds up to a multiple of 2048, so a group holds at most 10,240). Recorded in release.json (row_group_rows, and the largest group written as row_group_rows_max).

overwrite

replace an existing dir_out/release/ (default FALSE: stop).

decades

decades (first year) to export in the decade layers; default 1960-2020. NULL exports every decade present.

esn

expected sample size for ES(n) in the decade layers; default 50 (as in the store).

place_collections

optional named list (or character vector), slug = the gazetteer collection's membership (a directory or URL, its membership.json, or anything obis_place_indicators() takes as membership), e.g. list(eez = "<gazetteer base>/eez"). Default NULL: no place layer.

place_exact

optional named list (or character vector), slug = the path of the collection's GeoParquet of polygons (place_id, WKB geometry, an optional area_km2), e.g. list(mr_eez = "<places-internal>/mr_eez/places.parquet"). Default NULL: no exact place layer. Needs place_exact_occ.

place_exact_occ

the occurrence parquet path(s)/glob(s) the exact place indicators are computed from (OBIS open data, nested or flat; see obis_place_indicators_exact()).

temp_dir, max_temp_dir_size

DuckDB spill directory and cap for the exact place computation (it runs in its own DuckDB instance with this memory_limit and threads).

memory_limit

optional DuckDB memory_limit (e.g. "24GB").

threads

optional DuckDB thread count (e.g. 8).

verbose

print progress and the summary (default TRUE).

Value

invisibly, a character vector of the files written (absolute paths).

Details

<dir_out>/<release>/
  release.json                              build metadata, row counts, layout, columns, file manifest
  all/res=<1..5>/data_0.parquet             idx_h3 (all taxa, all years)
  all/res=<6,7>/p=<parent>/data_0.parquet   the fine res, one file per parent cell
  eov/eov=<eov>/res=<r>/data_0.parquet      idx_h3_eov
  taxon/rank=<rank>/taxon=<taxon>/res=<r>/  idx_h3_taxon (phylum / class / order / family),
                                            plus the heads (kingdom, subphylum, superclass ...)
  decade/all/decade=<yyy0>/res=<r>/         per decade, all taxa  (res in res_decade)
  decade/eov/eov=<eov>/decade=<yyy0>/res=<r>/  per decade and EOV (res in res_decade)
  year/all/year=<yyyy>/res=<r>/             per year, all taxa    (res in res_year)
  year/eov/eov=<eov>/year=<yyyy>/res=<r>/   per year and EOV      (res in res_year)
  species/res=<r>/class=<class>/data_0.parquet  species x hex x count (res in res_species)
  species/species.parquet                   the species lookup: names, name_key, lineage
  species/heads.json                        the pre-aggregated heads and the layer serving each
  species_decade/res=<r>/decade=<d>/class=<class>/  per decade (species_decades = TRUE)
  place/coll=<slug>/data_0.parquet          per-place pooled indicators (only with place_collections)
  place_exact/coll=<slug>/indicators.parquet, years.parquet, meta.json
                                            exact point-in-polygon indicators (only with place_exact)
  collection.json                           STAC Collection (h3 profile), obis_h3_stac_collection()
  stats.parquet                             value ranges per layer x key x period x res x variable
  taxon_groups.parquet                      the taxa and EOVs available, with totals and paths
  files.parquet                             manifest: layer, path, url_path, rows, bytes per file

Every indicator file has the columns h3 (lowercase hex string), cell_id, n, sp, shannon, simpson, es; the partition keys live in the path (read with hive_partitioning = true). Its rows are sorted by cell_id in row groups of row_group_rows (about 10k), so a reader that knows the cells under a tile reads only the row groups whose cell_id statistics overlap them (a range read) instead of the whole file. Each file is written by its own COPY (obis_h3_write_partitions()), since DuckDB's PARTITION_BY does not keep the order. The decade layers are computed from occ_h3 with the same SQL builder as idx_h3 / idx_h3_eov (so the math is identical to the store): n = records, sp = distinct species, Shannon, Simpson and ES(esn), grouped by cell and decade = floor(date_year / 10) * 10; records without a year are left out of the decade layers. EOV membership is the store's eov table (occ_h3.aphiaid = eov.taxonID), as in obis_eov_bake(). Layers whose source tables are missing (e.g. no idx_h3_eov in a store without taxonomy) are skipped with a message.

Partition values are percent-encoded by DuckDB (a space becomes %20), and DuckDB decodes them on read. A static web server decodes the URL once, so a browser must request the on-disk name with % itself encoded (%2520); taxon_groups.parquet carries both path (on disk) and url_path (to fetch), and files.parquet lists every file with both forms. Each partition is exactly one data_0.parquet.

Parent partitions for the fine resolutions. A whole res-7 layer is tens of MB, too much for a browser to load at once, so the resolutions named in parent_res are split by parent cell: every row of all/res=7/ goes to all/res=7/p=<h3 of its res-3 parent>/data_0.parquet (default res 6 by its res-2 parent, res 7 by its res-3 parent), and a viewer loads only the parent cells that cover its viewport. The taxon layer uses parent_res_taxon (default the res-0 base cell: res-3 parents would make over a million files across ~5k taxa). A (layer key, res) with at most parent_min_rows rows stays one whole file, since splitting it would only add requests. The decade layers are never split (their default resolutions are 1-5). files.parquet has a parent column (the partition's parent cell, NULL for a whole file; its resolution is the parent resolution), and each layer in release.json lists the parent_res actually used.

Place layer (optional). With place_collections, each gazetteer collection gets one file, place/coll=<slug>/data_0.parquet, with the indicators of every place pooled from its res-7 member cells, records weighted by each cell's share of area inside the place (obis_place_indicators()): columns place_id, layer (all | eov), key (” or the EOV), decade (NULL = all years, else the decades above), n (fractional), sp, shannon, simpson, es, cells, area. These are true per-place indices of the pooled, area-weighted counts, not means of hexagon values. The files are listed in files.parquet (layer place) and release.json (layers$place, with each collection's membership version); stats.parquet does not cover them.

Exact place layer (optional). With place_exact, each polygon collection gets place_exact/coll=<slug>/indicators.parquet and years.parquet (obis_place_indicators_exact(), written by obis_place_exact_write()): the indicators of every place computed from the OBIS occurrences inside the true polygon, with no H3 approximation, per EOV (all and the store's eov table), per decade and per year, with Berger-Parker and density. They are values only (no geometry), computed from the occurrence parquet files place_exact_occ (the local snapshot the store was built from), which takes far longer than the layers above. The files are listed in files.parquet (layer place_exact) and release.json (layers$place_exact, with each collection's places and record totals); stats.parquet does not cover them.

Year layers. year/all and year/eov are the decade layers per year: the same SQL (obis_h3_year_sql()) grouped by year = date_year, one partition per year present from min(date_year) to max(date_year) (or the years asked for), at the resolutions res_year (default 1-5, never split by parent). release.json lists the years written (years).

The species table (species/, spike 2 of the Ocean Metrics restructure): one row per (cell, aphiaid) with n = records, at the resolutions res_species (default 3, 4, 5; res 4 rolled up from the res-5 tier), so a browser answers a WoRMS subtree or "which species are in this cell" from static files. Columns h3, cell_id, name_key, aphiaid, n (obis_h3_species_sql()); one data_0.parquet per (res, class) written by obis_h3_write_partitions(), sorted by cell_id, aphiaid in row groups of 100k; a NULL class is class=_none. species/species.parquet (obis_h3_species_lookup_sql()) has one row per aphiaid with its names, a name_key per distinct name (richness counts names) and its lineage (self, then ancestors up the store's taxon table); a subtree is list_contains(lineage, <aphiaid>) (obis_h3_species_subtree_sql()). species/heads.json lists the taxa that need a pre-aggregated head (obis_h3_species_heads(): Animalia and every taxon spanning two or more named classes) and the layer that serves each.

The heads (heads = TRUE) are written as ordinary taxon layers, taxon/rank=<rank>/taxon=<name>/res=<r>/ at res_heads (obis_h3_heads_sql(): the WoRMS subtree from the lineage, species counted by name_key, so a head equals obis_h3_species_subtree_sql() cell for cell), where rank is the WoRMS rank lowercased without a botanical alias ("Phylum (Division)" is phylum). They then appear in stats.parquet, taxon_groups.parquet and files.parquet as any taxon. A head is not written when a layer already serves it: one whose subtree holds every aphiaid (and the store has no record without one) is the all layer; one whose rank and name are a rank layer of idx_h3_taxon keeps that layer (built from the OBIS rank column, not the WoRMS subtree, so it may differ in a few cells). heads.json gives each head's served_by (head, all, rank_layer, or homonym for a second taxon with the same rank and name) and its layer. The per-decade variant species_decade/ is written only with species_decades = TRUE. Rows with no aphiaid are left out; a store without one (e.g. the demo store built from occ_SAtlantic) gets no species layer.

collection.json is a STAC Collection of the release for the Ocean Metrics h3 profile (obis_h3_stac_collection()).

stats.parquet has one row per indicator layer and (key, decade, year, res, variable) with min, p02, p50, p98, max and n_cells (cells with a non-NULL value; a variable NULL everywhere in a partition gets a row with NULL ranges and n_cells 0), for colour ramps. key is the EOV or taxon name (” for the all-taxa layers), rank the taxon rank (” otherwise), decade NA outside the decade layers, year NA outside the year layers.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- obis_store_connect("~/data/obis/obis_h3.duckdb")
obis_h3_export_parquet(con, "~/data/obis-h3", "v20260728")
} # }
